posts.title: Viewing Mill Cross Yard at five in the morning
posts.excerpt: A flower wholesaler wanted north light and a 05:00 loading slot, so we viewed Bay 7 at that hour.
posts.content:
A flower wholesaler came to Hashira Partners with a short brief and a precise clock. They wanted north light and a loading slot at 05:00. The goods were flowers. The floor they were willing to use was a cold one. They did not ask for a cold store. We would not have had one to offer. The firm does not handle cold stores, hazardous storage, or a bay larger than 420 m².

The building that matched the light and the hour was Mill Cross Yard, in Mill Cross. The yard has 10 bays, from 150 to 300 m², with a clear height of 6.5 m. Rent starts at $11 per m² per month. It sits between steel-clad sheds. The bay in the note is Bay 7, at 240 m². The concept we wrote down is early mornings, cold floors. The type is cool dispatch. Tomasz Wrona is the agent for Mill Cross, so the visit sat with him.

Before that morning, the path was the ordinary one. Tell us the size, the district and when you need it. We reply within 1 business day. Priya Raman then holds a 20-minute call to narrow the list to 3 bays. Three is the shape of the first viewing round. That round is free and takes about 2 hours, with an agent and, where possible, the owner. Bay 7 was on the short list because 240 m² sits inside the yard's range, and because the wholesaler's real question was the hour.

Published viewing hours are Tue–Sat 09:00–15:00. Office hours, when a reply is written, are Mon–Fri 08:30–17:30. For this firm the useful hour was 05:00, the loading slot they wanted to judge. A flower wholesaler wanted north light and a 05:00 loading slot, so we viewed the yard at that hour. The light was the early light they had asked about. The floor was cold concrete. Cool dispatch, in this note, means flowers across an ordinary warehouse floor at the start of the day. It does not mean a refrigerated store.

The check was the check we make on any round. Measure the shutter, walk the loading route, test the power. The measurement answers whether the load can pass that opening. The walk, taken at the real hour, shows whether the yard works while the street is quiet. The power test is a test of that unit on that day. Clear height at Mill Cross Yard is 6.5 m. Had the work needed 8 m, the building to name would have been Foundry Court in Eastgate, where a separate note concerns one large machine. Foundry Court has 6 bays, from 200 to 420 m², a clear height of 8 m, and rent from $11 per m² per month. Bay 2 there is 320 m².

Daniel Cho, our building surveyor, checks a floor when the use needs a rating. He did so before terms at Bay 2, Foundry Court, where a print finisher needed 8 m clear and a floor rated for its folder. The flower brief did not ask for that check. A written floor and loading check report is still a published item at $340, for a firm that wants the check on paper. Lucía Ferrer, our lease clerk, reads the heads of terms through with you if a bay fits. That lease read-through is $480. Those are separate lines from the visit. The visit was there so the bay could be seen properly: shutter, floor, light and, where possible, the owner in the room.

An empty bay is a beginning when the person who might work there has stood in it, and when the owner can answer for the building. We do not add a move-in date to the note, or a saving, or a rating. We publish the bay and the use. The project line is Bay 7, Mill Cross Yard, 240 m². A reader can see the ask and the conditions. A reader should not treat the note as word that Bay 7 is free next month, or that every flower firm will want the same yard.

The rest of the portfolio stays in view so one morning does not stand in for the firm. We lease 50 bays across 6 buildings, from 90 to 420 m². Tanner Row Sheds in Eastgate has 12 bays at 90 to 180 m², clear height 6 m, rent from $12 per m² per month. Quay Lane Units in Riverside has 8 bays at 120 to 240 m², clear height 5.5 m, rent from $14. Ferry Road Depot, also Riverside, has 9 bays at 100 to 220 m², clear height 5 m, rent from $13. Orchard Street Works in Mill Cross has 5 bays at 90 to 160 m², clear height 4.5 m, rent from $15. Adaeze Nwosu covers Riverside and Ferry Road. A first round can set a Riverside bay beside a Mill Cross bay when the call supports it.

If a lease is signed, the placement fee is paid only once. Placement fee, lease up to 24 months: 1 month's rent. Placement fee, lease of 25 months or more: 1.5 months' rent. Listing a bay is free for an owner. Henrik Aas handles that conversation. The early viewing was not a special product with its own price. It was the work of showing a bay at the hour the work starts. A firm that needs that should say so in the request, with the size and the district.

We will reply within 1 business day from Unit 4, 18 Tanner Row, Port Merrin. The address is viewings@hashirapartners.example and the phone is 555-0142. Mika Hashira founded the firm in 2014 for this kind of showing: small bays, looked at properly, with the facts of the building left as they are.
